Pick a Map

BO6 launched with two maps and added one per season until Reckoning closed the story in Season 5. Play in release order for the Dark Aether storyline — the crew, the Sentinel Artifact and S.A.M. carry from map to map. Difficulty is about the main quest, not survival.

Before You Drop In

The stuff that works on every map — learn it once, use it six times.

New to BO6 Zombies? Start on Liberty Falls in Directed Mode — it walks you through the main quest with on-screen objectives and caps the round so the horde never out-scales you while you learn. Side easter eggs are switched off in Directed Mode, so graduate to Standard once the steps feel familiar.

How BO6 Zombies Works

Everything on this page works identically on all six maps. Learn it once here, then each map guide only has to teach you what's different.

Modes

ModeWhat it isPick it when
StandardThe full experience — main quest, side easter eggs, Intel, no round cap.You know the steps, or you're hunting side content.
DirectedMain quest only, with on-screen objectives and a round cap that holds the difficulty while you work. Side easter eggs are disabled.First time doing any map's main quest. Always learn here first.

Essence, Salvage & The Upgrade Chain

  • Essence is your points — kills, hits and round bonuses. It buys doors, perks, Pack-a-Punch and armor.
  • Salvage drops from zombies and is spent at the Arsenal (weapon rarity + ammo mods) and the Crafting Table (equipment and support).
  • Pack-a-Punch has three tiers — 5,000 / 15,000 / 30,000 Essence — each massively raising damage and magazine size. A Tier III weapon is the entry ticket to every boss fight in this guide.
  • Weapon rarity at the Arsenal (Uncommon → Rare → Epic → Legendary) stacks with Pack-a-Punch. Boss-ready means Tier III + Legendary.
  • Armor comes in tiers at armor wall-buys; plates are refilled from drops and the Crafting Table. Never start a boss fight without full plates and a spare set.
Spending order that wins runs: doors to Pack-a-Punch → Jugger-Nog → Tier I Pack → armor → Speed Cola / Quick Revive → rarity at the Arsenal → Tier II/III Pack → the rest of your perks from Der Wunderfizz.

All 11 Perk-a-Colas — And The Augments To Run

Each perk you buy raises the price of the next one, so buy in priority order. Der Wunderfizz (on every map) sells a random perk — and once you own several, it can hand you the rest. Every perk has 3 Major + 3 Minor augments to research; you equip one of each. The picks below are the community-standard best combos.

PerkBase effectRun these augments
Jugger-Nog+100 max health. Buy it first, every run.Major: Probiotic (even more health) · Minor: Hardened Plates (armor mitigates more)
Quick ReviveHealth regen delay cut 50%; revive allies 50% faster. In solo it's your safety net.Major: Dying Wish solo (survive a lethal hit at 1 HP) / EMT in co-op (revived allies keep their perks) · Minor: Karmic Return
Speed ColaReload and armor replating 30% faster.Major: Classic Formula (reload even faster) · Minor: Quick Swap
Stamin-UpFaster movement and sprint. Essential for boss arenas and training.Major: Dasher or Stalker · Minor: Hard Target (less projectile damage while tac-sprinting)
Deadshot DaiquiriADS snaps to critical spots; bonus critical damage. The camo-grind perk.Critical-damage augments — research whatever you unlock first, it all feeds headshots.
PhD FlopperImmune to your own explosive/splash damage and fall damage; diving to prone detonates a blast that scales with fall height.Slide/flopper-blast augments. Mandatory for explosive builds and several boss fights.
Elemental PopEvery shot has a chance to trigger a random ammo-mod effect.Pairs with any ammo mod; better the deeper your augment research is across mods.
Melee MacchiatoReplaces your gun-butt with a heavy punch that launches zombies. New to BO6 — and a real quest tool (it opens things on Citadelle and Reckoning).Melee damage augments for early-round one-punch kills.
Death PerceptionSee enemies, loot and items through walls; minimap pings threats. Added after launch.Quality-of-life pick for Intel and loot hunting.
Double TapGreatly increased fire rate. The classic returns — added after launch and an instant top-tier pick for boss DPS.Fire-rate augments; grab it whenever Wunderfizz offers it.
Vulture AidZombies drop extra ammo, Essence and Salvage pickups. Added after launch.The economy perk — huge on high rounds and camo grinds.

GobbleGums

Build a pack of GobbleGums in the pre-game Loadout menu. In a match, the Mr. Peeks machine hands you a random gum from your pack — free, on a cooldown that grows each use. You can hold up to three at once. Gums are earned just by playing (roughly one every few rounds) and unused gums are never lost. There are three trigger types — Instant, Timed and Conditional — and five rarities:

  • Ultra — game-changers. Perkaholic (every perk on the map, instantly), Wonderbar! (next Mystery Box spin is guaranteed a Wonder Weapon), Reign Drops (spawns every power-up at once), Near Death Experience is Legendary — see below.
  • Legendary — Phoenix Up (revives the whole squad, they keep perks), Near Death Experience (revive by standing near a downed teammate), Idle Eyes (zombies freeze for 30 seconds), Hidden Power (instant Pack-a-Punch on your current weapon).
  • Epic — Free Fire (no ammo drain for 60s), Soda Fountain (next perk buy gives a bonus free perk), Temporal Gift (power-ups last longer).
  • Rare — Shields Up (double-strength armor for 3 minutes), Kill Joy (spawns an Insta-Kill), Cache Back (spawns a Max Ammo), Stock Option (fire from your stockpile ammo), Anywhere But Here (emergency teleport).
  • Whimsical — joke gums (Newtonian Negation flips gravity effects on kills). Fun, zero power.

Easter Egg Pack

Perkaholic · Timeout · Phoenix Up · Arsenal Accelerator · Kill Joy · Shields Up

The official recommended shape for quest attempts: free perks, a breather button, a squad-save, faster upgrades.

Boss Fight Pack

Idle Eyes · Reign Drops · Near Death Experience · Free Fire · Shields Up

Freeze the adds, drop every power-up, and keep the squad standing through the final phase.

High Round Pack

Perkaholic · Wonderbar! · Stock Option · Temporal Gift · Cache Back

Economy and ammo sustain for round 50+ — plus a Wonder Weapon reroll when yours falls off.

Enemies — And How To Drop Them

EnemyWhereCounter
Zombie / Armored / HeavyEverywhereHeadshots scale best; armored zombies need their helmets broken first — Deadshot earns its keep.
HellhoundSpecial rounds on several mapsKeep moving; they lunge in packs. A shotgun or melee ends the round fast.
VerminTerminus, Tomb, Veil, ReckoningSmall, fast, low. Hip-fire and Cryo Freeze; don't ADS at your feet.
ParasiteCitadelle, The TombFlying and spits acid. Shoot them first — they also charge the Solais sword on Citadelle.
ManglerAll maps (elite)Shoot the arm cannon to stop the barrage, then the head. Napalm Burst melts them.
AbominationLiberty Falls (elite)Shoot the glowing mouths when they open; never fight it in a doorway.
AmalgamTerminus (elite)Grabs and pulls you in — kill it at range, break line of sight to stop the grab.
DoppelghastCitadelle, Shattered Veil (special)Fast and tanky; it drops quest items on both maps, so don't exfil past one.
Elder DiscipleShattered Veil (elite)Buffs nearby zombies and drains you — priority target, burst it down first.
Kommando KlausReckoning (special)Flying Janus robot. Shoot the shoulder joints — its arms are a quest item.
Toxic ZombieReckoningExplodes into a gas cloud on death. Kill at range, don't train through the cloud.

Power-ups & Exfil

  • Max Ammo, Insta-Kill, Double Points, Nuke, Full Power, Bonus Points, Fire Sale — every map also hides a free set of power-ups you can spawn by shooting hidden Mr. Peeks figures/objects; each map guide lists its set.
  • Exfil is first offered at round 11, then every five rounds. Clear the exfil zone before the timer ends for bonus Essence and XP — or decline and keep pushing.
  • S.A.M. Trials spawn on every map: short challenges for rarity upgrades, free perks and gear. Worth it early, skippable late.
  • Rampage Inducer (the orange canister near spawn) speeds up spawns and zombie speed until round 20 — the camo grinder's best friend, the beginner's worst enemy.

Terminus
Launch Map · Philippine Sea

Terminus

A Project Janus prison island. The Requiem crew — Weaver, Grey, Carver and Maya — breaks out of the holding cells, restores power to the facility, and goes looking for a way off the island. What Janus was keeping in the Bio Lab has other ideas. Main quest: “No Mo' Modi.”

MapMain QuestBeamsmasherBossSide Eggs & Intel

Interactive Map — The Mission Route

The real in-game tac-map of Terminus Island. Numbered pins are the main quest in the order you run it — follow 1 to 10 and you walk the whole mission. Lettered pins are side missions. Tap any pin to open its step.

Tap a pin

Numbered pins run the “No Mo' Modi” main quest in order. Lettered pins are side missions and secrets.

Main Quest — “No Mo' Modi”

Seven stages. The Beamsmasher is not optional — the quest hard-requires it — so build it early (next section) instead of gambling on the Mystery Box.

  1. Power the island. Activate all three AMP Generators (Guard Station, Living Quarters, Engineering), defending each while it charges. Then head to the Bio Lab and raise the submerged Pack-a-Punch lift for 500 Essence.
  2. Get the DRI-11 Beamsmasher. Mystery Box luck, a Wonderbar! gum, or build it — full build below.
  3. Recover the Hard Drive. Fire the Beamsmasher's beam into an active Tentacle Trap — use the one with the damaged vent / glowing particles — and pull the Hard Drive out. Deliver it to Peck at the Guard Station (drop it in the postbox slot).
  4. Free Nathan. Three clues around the facility give you a three-digit code: the clock in the Quick Revive area (hour hand), the playing card in the Mess Hall (card value), and the “days since injury” sign in Engineering. Enter the code on Nathan's containment unit in the Bio Lab, then have every player turn a relief valve at the same time. Kill the elite Nathan that comes out, then dive to his body underwater and take the Keycard.
  5. Reconnect the nodes. Use the Keycard, survive the Shipwreck lockdown, and carry the two Node Connectors to the broken nodes to restore the network.
  6. Hack the buoys, defuse the bombs. Take Peck's Hacking Device out by boat and hack the three sea buoys (north, southeast, southwest) — each hack is a timed defense. Then get back to the Bio Lab and defuse the three bombs before their timer runs out.
  7. Kill Patient 13. Gear up fully (below), then open the big white door at the bottom of the Bio Lab. Everyone votes to enter — there's no leaving until it's dead.

Wonder Weapon — DRI-11 Beamsmasher (Build)

Aetheric beam weapon: the primary fire slows and melts groups, the alternate mode stuns. Three parts, all gated behind the AMP generators and Pack-a-Punch:

  1. EMF Fob. Put Dead Wire on any weapon (Arsenal). Ride the Bio Lab Pack-a-Punch lift upward and shoot the electrical boxes through the slanted windows as you pass, following the current as it jumps from the Bio Lab toward Living Quarters and the Rec Yard, until the final box drops the EMF Fob.
  2. AMP Munition & Hardened Cables. The remaining parts come from around the island — a Mangler-related drop and the Engineering/Storage areas. Directed Mode markers point at each one in order; in Standard, sweep Engineering and Storage after the Fob and listen for Peck's radio hints.
  3. Assemble at the workbench in the Bio Lab area. Pack-a-Punch it as soon as you can — the quest's later steps assume you have it.

Boss Fight — Patient 13

  • Bring: Tier III Pack-a-Punch + Legendary rarity on your main weapon, all perks you can carry, Tier III armor, a Mutant Injection or Chopper Gunner in reserve, PhD Flopper and Jugger-Nog non-negotiable.
  • Phase 1 — shoulders. Shoot the glowing red bulbs on its shoulders. Dodge the two-arm slam in front of it — it hits for around 200 damage.
  • Phase 2 — mouth. After a mini-boss wave, weak point moves to the mouth. Watch the tongue sweep across the back of the arena.
  • Phase 3 — eyes & mouth (from ~25% HP). The arena closes in and it gains two killers: a tongue grab that pulls you into its mouth for a down, and an electric wipe attack — when your screen fills with blue wisps and its arms rise sparking, get behind cover until the orb bursts. Then pour fire into the blue eyes, red bulbs and open mouth.
  • Ammo discipline wins this fight. Kill adds for drops between phases; don't burn your wonder weapon ammo on the horde.

Side Easter Eggs & Intel

  • Mega Stuffy: find the stuffed animals hidden around the island and assemble them at the bunk in Living Quarters for a friendly helper.
  • Cursed Talisman: a multi-step secret that trades your Essence gain for a permanent damage buff — a high-round hardcore option.
  • Free power-ups: like every BO6 map, Terminus hides a full set of shootable Mr. Peeks power-ups (Max Ammo, Insta-Kill, Nuke and more) — check the docks, the sea caves and under the shipwreck.
  • Boat & sea caves: the tactical raft is free transport — the caves hold loot, an AMP generator route, and several Intel pieces.
  • Intel: audio logs, documents and artifacts are scattered through the Guard Station, Research offices and Bio Lab — sweep offices while generators charge.

Sources: Terminus main quest steps — mmonster · No Mo' Modi walkthrough — codzombiesguides

Citadelle des Morts
Season 1 · Avalon, France

Citadelle des Morts

After Terminus, the crew follows Ravenov's lead to a castle in Avalon controlled by the French Syndicate, hunting Gabriel Krafft — the one man who can lead them to the Sentinel Artifact. This is BO6's longest, most puzzle-dense quest: four swords, four incantations, one Guardian. Completing it in Standard Mode awards the Jackknife Weaver operator skin.

MapMain QuestSwords & IncantationsBossSide Eggs & Intel

Interactive Map — The Mission Route

The real in-game tac-map — castle at the top, village below. Numbered pins are the main quest in run order; lettered pins are side missions. Tap a pin to open its step.

Tap a pin

Numbered pins run the main quest in order. Lettered pins are side missions and secrets.

Main Quest — At A Glance

  1. Open the castle & Pack-a-Punch. Fire the courtyard cannon at the castle entrance. In the Dungeon, break the locks on the metal box, kill the Doppelghast that spawns, and take the Blood Aetherium Crystal. Place it at the red-glowing container to reveal Pack-a-Punch.
  2. Talk to Krafft. In the Dungeon near Quick Revive, interact with the cell door to speak with Gabriel Krafft — this officially starts the quest.
  3. Claim all four Bastard Swords and upgrade each into its elemental form (next section).
  4. Earn all four Incantations by completing each sword's ritual-item hunt (next section).
  5. Repair the book. Collect the torn page fragments, restore the book in the Alchemical Lab, and read the Points of Power trap order it reveals — activate the traps in sequence to advance.
  6. Honor the knights. In the Dining Hall, inspect each knight statue with its matching sword + incantation equipped. Read the symbol code around the orb holder (Dragon, Stag, Raven, Lion — I–II–III–IV).
  7. Charge the Mystic Orb. Complete the four elemental challenges with the orb — Dark in the Undercroft, Electric in the Town Square, Fire in the Courtyard, Light in the Dining Hall.
  8. Take the Guardian Key. Place the charged orb in the animal wall in the Alchemical Lab to open the secret study. Play the recording on the stone table and pick up the Guardian Key.
  9. Wake the Guardian. Insert the key at the statue in the Town Square (spawn). Point of no return — gear up first.

The Four Swords & Incantations

From round 10, zombies wearing Templar helmets drop stamps. Carry one stamp (only one at a time) to a knight statue in the Dining Hall to draw that knight's plain Bastard Sword, then upgrade it:

SwordUpgradeIncantation ritual item
Caliburn — Dragon (Fire)Place the sword at the dragon statue pedestal in the Entrance Hall/courtyard and light it from the three dragon-fire braziers.Ra's Ankh: light the three bonfires with Molotovs; kill the Doppelghast that spawns. Ritual symbol: Courtyard.
Durendal — Stag (Electric)Collect three lightning rods (one from a zombie in the storm, others around the ramparts/village), place them in the urn on the Hillside Ramparts, and let lightning charge the sword.Pegasus Horseshoe: shoot the horseshoe above the barn to start a storm, then pick it up where it lands. Ritual symbol: Town Square.
Balmung — Raven (Dark)Take the sword and a fossil into the tavern cellar's circular puzzle; escort the three purple orbs to the portal — three rounds of it — to claim Balmung.Raven's Talon: on the dungeon cave slide, shoot the raven perched on the rock. Ritual symbol: Undercroft.
Solais — Lion (Light)Kill a glowing Parasite to charge the sword, melee the four lion-head door knockers in the upper village underpass, then shoot the sanctuary symbols in the order shown.Paladin Brooch: redirect the light beam from the crystal in the Dining Hall onto the busts (six redirects). Ritual symbol: Dining Hall.
How incantations work: place the ritual item on its glowing symbol, get kills in the circle until a chest rises, then melee the chest open with the matching sword. You carry incantations as tactical-slot charges — and you'll need all four stocked for the boss.

Boss Fight — The Guardian

  • The Town Square statue is the Guardian. Inserting the key teleports you to a sealed arena that slowly floods with lava, shrinking your safe ground as the fight goes on.
  • Damage comes from weak points: shoot the glowing parts of its armor — start by breaking the seal on its back (get behind it), then work the glowing joints as they expose. In the final phase, only the chest weak point counts.
  • Incantation crates spawn mid-arena with charges for all four elements, plus an ammo box — rotate incantations on the adds and save your gun ammo for the boss.
  • Bring a Tier III gun for adds, keep moving as lava rises, and don't get caught admiring the hammer slam — its AoE is the fight's biggest killer.

Side Easter Eggs & Intel

  • Light Mend ammo mod debuts on this map — Citadelle is where you unlock its research.
  • Wisps & the well: several small secrets hide around the village well, the tavern and the castle ramparts — check every fireplace and bookshelf for Intel.
  • Free power-ups: a hidden Mr. Peeks set is scattered across the village and castle, same as every BO6 map.
  • Intel: the castle is dense with audio logs and documents — Krafft's cell, the Alchemical Lab and the Dining Hall are the richest rooms.

Shattered Veil
Season 3 · Colton Hall, West Virginia

Shattered Veil

Edward Richtofen's mansion — Colton Hall — looms over Liberty Falls, with a Project Janus lab in the basement and the S.A.M. AI waiting in the Mainframe Chamber. The crew brings her the Sentinel Artifact from The Tomb. The mansion's T-Rex skeleton has opinions about that.

MapMain QuestRay Gun Mark IIBossSide Eggs & Intel

Interactive Map — The Mission Route

The real in-game tac-map of Colton Hall — mansion upper right, Garden Pond spawn lower left. (The Mainframe Chamber is one floor down, reached by the elevator at pin 4.) Numbered pins are the main quest in run order; lettered pins are side missions. Tap a pin to open its step.

Tap a pin

Numbered pins run the main quest in order. Lettered pins are side missions and secrets.

Main Quest — At A Glance

  1. Repair the elevator, unlock Pack-a-Punch. From the Garden Pond spawn, push into the mansion. Kill the Maintenance Worker zombie in the Library for the Fuse, and shoot the flashing computer in the Director's Quarters for the Circuit Board. Install both in the elevator and ride down to the Mainframe Chamber — Pack-a-Punch and S.A.M. are waiting.
  2. Get the Ray Gun Mark II. From round 10, a Lab Technician spawns in the Mainframe Chamber — kill him for a Floppy Disk. Insert it in the fax machine in the East Foyer to print a four-letter code (it'll be a word like CRAB, YETI or WORM). Convert the word to numbers using the chalkboard in the Nursery (letters map to the numbers beneath them), then enter the code on the keypad to free the Doppelghast and claim the Mark II.
  3. Build all three Mark II variants — W, P and R (next section). Each one unlocks a Liminal Space ritual.
  4. Complete the three Liminal Trials. Charge each variant at its painting/computer stations around the mansion, step through its portal, and beat the trial — including the Liminal bosses (the Distillery trial ends with Hogsimi; the Library trial with Yavax'Tul). Each finished trial charges the Sentinel Artifact further.
  5. Face the Z-Rex. With the Artifact fully charged, place it in the machine in front of S.A.M. in the Mainframe Chamber. Final prep below — there's no coming back to shop.

Wonder Weapons — Ray Gun Mark II & Its Variants

  • Base Mark II: three-round burst, penetrates targets, bigger magazine than the classic Ray Gun. Quest-built as above, or from the Mystery Box / Wonderbar!.
  • Mark II-W (blue): the boss-killer — full-auto energy with the best Z-Rex damage of the three. Build it via the canister + waterfall/garden ritual route.
  • Mark II-P (purple): psychic variant with a charged shot; needed for its painting station and Liminal Trial.
  • Mark II-R (yellow): radiation variant; needed for the Library-side steps and its trial.
  • Also on this map: the Wunderwaffe DG-2 returns via its own build/Box luck — superb crowd control for the boss arena. You can only carry so much: Mark II-W + Wunderwaffe is the meta boss loadout; the AMR Mod 4 sniper (Tier III, Legendary) is the budget alternative that hits nearly as hard.

Boss Fight — Z-Rex

  • The Main Hall's T-Rex skeleton comes alive in a wide arena — this is a movement fight. Stamin-Up and PhD Flopper are close to mandatory; keep sprinting between its stomps and bites.
  • Shoot the glowing weak points as they expose along its body; between phases it speeds up and hits harder, and the horde never stops coming.
  • Bring: Tier III Mark II-W (or Tier III Legendary AMR Mod 4), Tier III armor, full perks, and crowd control in the equipment slots — Gersch Devices / Monkey Bombs if you have them, and GobbleGums like Idle Eyes or Near Death Experience (co-op) are proven picks here.
  • Rewards on completion: the ending cutscene, plus a loot haul — Tier III Pack-a-Punch crystal, a Ray Gun, an Epic Aether Tool, Essence, Salvage and a free Perkaholic.

Side Easter Eggs & Intel

  • Free Jet Gun: a Jet Gun is obtainable on this map and is genuinely useful in the Z-Rex fight for add control.
  • Death Perception and Vulture Aid joined the perk roster around this map's season — check Der Wunderfizz here if you're missing them elsewhere.
  • Free power-ups: the hidden Mr. Peeks set returns — the mansion's chimneys, the garden and the service tunnels are the usual hiding spots.
  • Intel: Richtofen's own home is stuffed with lore — the Director's Quarters, Library and Nursery hold the best of it.

Reckoning
Season 5 · Janus Towers — The Finale

Reckoning

Project Janus's twin towers — the birthplace of S.A.M. — rise over Liberty Falls. Everything from five maps of story lands here: Eddie and S.A.M. are on opposing sides now, and for the first time in BO6, the ending is a vote. Help S.A.M. and you fight Uber Richtofen. Help Richtofen and you fight S.A.M.

MapMain QuestGorgofex & KlausBoss — Two EndingsSide Eggs & Intel

Interactive Map — The Mission Route

The real in-game tac-map — this is the Sublevel 10 floor, home of the Particle Accelerator and Pack-a-Punch. Janus Towers stacks several floors, so each pin's step names its floor. Numbered pins are the main quest in run order; lettered pins are side missions. Tap a pin to open its step.

Tap a pin

Numbered pins run the main quest in order. Lettered pins are side missions and secrets.

Main Quest — At A Glance

  1. Grab the bucket. Seriously — pick up the mop bucket near spawn before anything else. You will need it much later and backtracking for it is miserable.
  2. Power & Pack-a-Punch. Fight down to Sublevel 10 and activate the Particle Accelerator — destroy the Aetherium shards around it to bring Pack-a-Punch online.
  3. Build Klaus. From about round 5–6, flying Kommando Klaus robots appear — shoot their shoulder joints to drop both arms. Assemble Klaus at his frame, then activate him with a Fowler Mutant Injection.
  4. Build the Gorgofex (next section) — the quest cannot proceed without it.
  5. Give Klaus the brain. With Melee Macchiato, punch the purple container in the Quantum Computing Core to free the brain, and carry it — on foot, no detours — to Klaus in the Teleportation Lab. Follow Klaus and complete the Fowler injection sequence.
  6. Wash the head. Fire a charged Gorgofex shot into the gap in the wall in Quantum Containment to knock down a zombie head. Meanwhile, set off the sprinklers (a Molotov at the smoke detector by the security room works), put the bucket under one, and cleanse the head in the wet bucket. Charge the cleansed head with zombie kills like a soul box and place it in the teleporter.
  7. Charge the Gorgofex. At the Pack-a-Punch room console, hit the big red button, survive the lockdown, and kill the blue Quantum Vermin with the Gorgofex until the pylon outside charges with a blue orb. Take the orb into the Gorgofex — then do not fire it until you've shot the teleporter in the T2 Teleportation Room with that charged shot.
  8. Catch the four purple objects. Loot Kazimir grenades from Janus containers around the towers and use them to capture the four floating purple objects scattered across the map. That opens the final portal.
  9. Choose your ending. At the Sentinel Artifact console, the squad votes: side with S.A.M. or with Richtofen. The boss — and the ending cutscene — depends on the vote.

Wonder Weapon — Gorgofex, And Your Robot, Klaus

  1. The periodic-table door. In the Mutant Research Lab, watch the static-filled monitors — they flash capital letters. Combine them into a chemical symbol, find that element's atomic number on the periodic table chart on the wall, pad it to three digits with a leading zero (e.g. 026), and punch it into the keypad to open the secret door.
  2. Inside: take the Gorgofex magazine, drain the Aether plants as directed, and survive the Uber Klaus it spawns — lead it toward your crafted Klaus if you want the two-for-one progress. Claim the Gorgofex.
  3. Honest review: the Gorgofex is a quest tool first and a weapon second — most squads carry it on one player and let everyone else run real DPS (AMR Mod 4, Jackal PDW, AK-74 are the proven boss guns here). Pack-a-Punch it at least once if it's your only special.
  4. Klaus is a teammate: once built and injected, Franken Klaus follows, fights, and is required for multiple quest beats — keep him alive and don't start steps without him nearby.

Boss Fight — Two Endings

  • Help Richtofen → fight S.A.M. (the easier fight). S.A.M. manifests as a massive Aether orb: shoot her four weak spots on the sphere, respect the laser beam, and farm the adds for armor plates between phases. Best guns: AMR Mod 4, Jackal PDW, Tanto, AK-74 — all Tier III.
  • Help S.A.M. → fight Uber Richtofen (the hardest boss in BO6). A jetpack-equipped Richtofen with a Wunderwaffe: Phase 1, shoot the shoulder pads on the ground. Phase 2, he takes flight with air raids and electric sniping. When he lands, never be underneath him — the landing crush is an instant down.
  • Either fight: the arena phases involve filling Ethereal Canisters (soul boxes) under fire, so go in with full plates, a stocked Aether Shroud, and a GobbleGum pack built for survival — Idle Eyes, Reign Drops, Near Death Experience.
  • Both endings complete the BO6 Zombies story and set up what comes next — do the other one on your second clear to see both cutscenes.

Side Easter Eggs & Intel

  • Caster Trap upgrade: the towers' Caster traps can be upgraded through a hidden multi-step secret — worth it for high rounds.
  • Paintings: interactive paintings around the Executive Suite and offices hide steps and Intel — check every frame.
  • Free power-ups: the Mr. Peeks set is here too, spread across both towers and Sublevel 10.
  • Intel: Maxis's personal effects in the Executive Suite and Director's Office are the emotional core of this map's collectibles — don't rush past them.

Sources: Reckoning Easter egg guide & rewards — DETONATED · Reckoning full Easter egg guide — The Nerd Stash

Camos & Grind
Progression

Camos, Augments & The Grind

The long-term chase in BO6 Zombies: mastery camos on every weapon, a full augment research tree, and the calling cards that come with them.

The Road To Nebula

Every weapon climbs the same ladder. Check the exact counters on the weapon's in-game challenge card — they vary slightly by weapon class.

  1. Military camos (9 per weapon): critical-kill (headshot) challenges, ending at 2,000 critical kills for the final military camo on most weapons. Liberty Falls with the Rampage Inducer on is the fastest farm in the game.
  2. Two Special camos per weapon: unlocked after the military set; each weapon has its own pair of conditions (elemental kills, rapid kills, point-blank, etc.).
  3. Mystic Gold: get 10 rapid kills, 15 times with the weapon.
  4. Opal: eliminate 30 Special zombies (Manglers, Doppelghasts and their kin) — requires Mystic Gold on that weapon first, and Opal on a set number of weapons before Afterlife opens per category.
  5. Afterlife: get 20 kills without taking damage, 10 times.
  6. Nebula: eliminate 10 Elite zombies (Abominations, Amalgams, Elder Disciples, bosses' mini-bosses) with the weapon. Nebula is account-flex: animated, and earned one weapon at a time.
Fastest loop: Liberty Falls, Directed or Standard, Rampage Inducer on, train at the bowling alley / Main Street, Deadshot Daiquiri + Vulture Aid, exfil or die around round 21 and repeat. Save & Quit (solo) preserves camo progress mid-run.

Augment Research — Priority Order

Research runs in the pre-game Augments menu: pick one Perk, Ammo Mod or Field Upgrade to research, and playing earns progress toward its 6 augments (3 Major, 3 Minor). Research these first — they pay off on every map:

  1. Jugger-Nog — Probiotic + Hardened Plates make every run safer.
  2. Quick Revive — Dying Wish (solo) and EMT (co-op) are run-savers.
  3. Aether Shroud — its augments extend your quest-step safety window; nearly every boss strategy assumes it.
  4. Speed Cola — Classic Formula speeds up everything, including camo-grind reload cycles.
  5. Deadshot Daiquiri — direct multiplier on the critical-kill grind.
  6. Stamin-Up & PhD Flopper — boss-arena survival kit.
  7. Then your favorite ammo mod (Dead Wire and Cryo Freeze first), and Melee Macchiato before serious Citadelle/Reckoning quest attempts.
